test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 19 Sept 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Carbon shows greater tendency for catenation than silicon.

Which of the following statements is the correct explanation for the given assertion?

options.text: Carbon-carbon bond is weaker than Si-Si bond due to the larger size of carbon as compared to silicon.
Carbon-carbon bond is weaker than Si-Si bond due to the smaller size of carbon as compared to silicon.
Carbon-carbon bond is stronger than Si-Si bond due to the larger size of carbon as compared to silicon.
Carbon-carbon bond is stronger than Si-Si bond due to the smaller size of carbon as compared to silicon.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Carbon-carbon bond is stronger than Si-Si bond due to the smaller size of carbon as compared to silicon. **__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Carbon exhibits catenation much more than silicon because of its smaller size.
 
• This makes C-C bond strong while the Si-Si bond are comparatively weaker due to its large size.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Catenation is the self-linking of atoms of an element to create chains and rings.
 
• Carbon is the most common element that exhibits catenation. It can form long hydrocarbon chains and rings like benzene.
